title: POC Hosting Choice: Mnemosyne Systems scoping
summary: Discovery + POC scoping to decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for inference. Captured success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, quality thresholds), baseline workload sizing, initial benchmark plan, timeline (8-10 weeks recommended), top risk: data residency and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: share security docs, run sample benchmark, price sketch and schedule on-prem tech deep dive.
topics: Workload characteristics: avg/peak QPS, sequence length
Success criteria: latency p95, throughput, quality acceptance
Decision factors: cost, SLA, data residency, integrations (SSO/KMS)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-06 11:30 PT / 14:30 ET, Duration 46m. Redwood AE: Jordan Lee, Redwood SE: Priya Nair. Mnemosyne: Carlos (CTO), Aisha (SRE), Liam (Product), Rina (Compliance).

[00:00:10] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we sent the agenda - quick intro on our side, i'm jordan lee, i'm the AE on the account. priya is our SE. could each of you do a 30 second intro?

[00:00:25] Carlos: yeah sure, carlos here, cto at mnemosyne. we run a multi-tenant analytics platform that enriches customer documents with LLMs. main concerns are latency for interactive features and strict data residency for e-comm clients.

[00:00:40] Aisha: aisha, sre. we own provisioning and runbooks. our constraints: predictable p99 latency, observability and audit trails.

[00:00:50] Liam: liam - product, building a semantic search + summarization feature, target is near real-time responses in the UI.

[00:01:00] Rina: rina, compliance, we need SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM integration for key material, and some EU-only customer contracts.

[00:01:15] Priya: thanks all. high level we want to help you pick between hosted, dedicated reserved pools, or a private (VPC/on-prem) deployment for the POC. we'll walk through tradeoffs and then scope a benchmark.

[00:02:05] Jordan: quick qualification Qs — what does your expected workload look like? avg qps and peak? typical token lengths?

[00:02:20] Carlos: we're currently seeing about 30 rps avg across all customers, peaks hitting 250 rps for short windows. our median prompt is 120 tokens, replies average 180 tokens.

[00:02:40] Aisha: concurrency with active user sessions is around 120 concurrent calls during peak. important to note the bulk of traffic is read-heavy (embeddings + generation).

[00:03:00] Priya: got it. any hard budget targets for latency or cost per 1M tokens?

[00:03:10] Liam: product wants interactive p95 under 350ms. Ops wants p99 under 800ms. Cost target is the rough equivalent of current infra spend; we don't have an exact per-token number yet, but want to avoid 3-4x uplift.

[00:03:30] Jordan: good. and data residency — EU-only customers?

[00:03:35] Rina: yes, about 18% of revenue is EU-restricted; data for those customers must remain in EU or on customer-managed keys.

[00:03:50] Priya: ok that nudges private or dedicated in-region for some customers; hosted can support regional routing but KMS/HSM and contract-level requirements push towards private in certain cases.

[00:04:15] Carlos: what about fallback/scale? we need graceful degradation so UI doesn't go dead.

[00:04:25] Priya: Redwood supports smart routing and automatic fallback to smaller-cap models or burst capacity; for hosted you can set fallbacks and routing policies. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput; private gives max control but increases ops surface.

[00:05:05] Jordan: let's dig into success criteria for the POC — what would success look like from your side?

[00:05:15] Liam: feature acceptance: search & summarization latency p95 < 350ms, relevance score delta < 5% vs baseline, and no data exfiltration risk.

[00:05:30] Carlos: infra acceptance: stable under 3x current peak for 1 hour (so ~750 rps), failover tested, and integration with our SSO and audit logs.

[00:05:45] Rina: compliance acceptance: SOC2 evidence for hosted or proof of managed logs and KMS for private/dedicated; contracts for EU residency.

[00:06:00] Priya: to translate, we should plan benchmarks for latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput ramp to 3x peak, quality evals against your test prompts, and a security checklist run.

[00:06:20] Jordan: timeline question — what's your preferred speed to decision?

[00:06:25] Carlos: we want something live-ish in 8–10 weeks if possible. pilot with a subset of customers, then expand.

[00:06:35] Priya: that aligns with a 6–10 week POC: week 1-2 onboarding + infra setup, week 3-5 benchmarking & tuning, week 6-8 integration and compliance docs, week 9-10 pilot run.

[00:07:00] Aisha: who handles model selection and benchmark scripts?

[00:07:05] Priya: we can supply benchmark harness and example prompts; we'll need a small dataset from you. we typically run: end-to-end API latencies, per-token cost, and relevance evals. we also can test quantized vs fp16 models to compare cost/latency.

[00:07:30] Liam: i want to make sure hallucination/regression is measured — can you run evals on a labeled set?

[00:07:40] Priya: yes, bring your labeled prompts/expected outputs; we'll run rouge/bertscore and a manual spot check.

[00:08:00] Jordan: let's sketch the hosting decision criteria matrix — we'll capture this and share. items: latency & throughput, cost delta, data residency/KMS, SLA & support, ops effort, rollout flexibility.

[00:08:20] Carlos: for us data residency and KMS are top 2, then latency, then cost. ops effort is tolerated if compliance demands it.

[00:08:35] Rina: also exportable audit logs and retention policy — we need 7 years for certain records.

[00:08:50] Priya: noted. hosted: fastest to run but limited KMS options unless hybrid keys via customer-managed keys? we do support customer-managed encryption keys for hosted in some regions but there are contract nuances. dedicated: reserved pools in specific regions, good middle ground — gives isolation and stronger contractual guarantees. private: VPC or on-prem — highest control for KMS and residency but highest ops and start time.

[00:09:40] Aisha: how about cost modeling — what's the typical approach?

[00:09:45] Priya: we model per-query cost based on token throughput, batching efficiency, and GPU utilization. for your workload with 120 token prompts + 180 token responses and concurrency of 120, at 250 rps peaks, we estimate X units — we'll run an exact model after we have sample traces.

[00:10:10] Carlos: can you give a rough ratio: hosted vs dedicated vs private?

[00:10:15] Jordan: ballpark: hosted sometimes 1.0x baseline (adds some margin for service), dedicated 0.9-1.2x depending on committed usage, private often 1.1-1.5x when you include ops and infra capital costs — but quantization and batching can shrink costs a lot.

[00:10:40] Liam: are there known perf regressions when moving from hosted to private?

[00:10:45] Priya: no inherent regression; performance is mostly determined by the hardware, kernel optimizations, and network topology. private can be faster if you place GPUs close to your app, but you lose some managed autoscaling features unless you implement them.

[00:11:10] Jordan: ok benchmark plan: Priya will run an initial microbenchmark in hosted to get baseline numbers (latency p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU util). then we'll repeat with a dedicated reserved pool with same model config; if needed we'll spin up a private VPC pilot in an EU region for the residency customers.

[00:11:40] Priya: for the microbenchmark we need: 1) sample prompt set (1000 prompts, distribution of seq lengths), 2) a small sandbox account or API key, 3) expected quality labels. we'll provide the harness and runner.

[00:12:00] Carlos: we'll provide traces and the labeled set, but keys might wait until contractual items are cleared.

[00:12:10] Jordan: that's fine — we can start with synthetic traces and our default models to get ballparks.

[00:12:25] Rina: for SOC2/ISO evidence — can you share your compliance pack and SOC2 report?

[00:12:30] Jordan: yes we'll share the SOC2 report and the security whitepaper. action: jordan to send sec pack.

[00:12:40] Aisha: KMS integration detail: do you support bringing your own key material with HSM-backed keys?

[00:12:45] Priya: for private deployments yes full KMS/HSM integration; for dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS via network peering or use Redwood-managed KMS with customer-supplied keys in some regions. hosted with BYOK is limited and requires contract amendments.

[00:13:15] Carlos: okay. network egress — we need to control egress over dedicated link/peering.

[00:13:20] Priya: supported — direct connect/peering is standard for dedicated and private.

[00:13:30] Liam: what about observability hooks? we need per-token cost breakdowns and request traces.

[00:13:40] Priya: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost, traces, and exportable logs. we'll show a demo if you'd like.

[00:13:55] Jordan: competition — any vendors you're evaluating?

[00:14:00] Carlos: looking at Anthropic enterprise and a few cloud-managed inference offerings, also MLOps teams that build on top of GPUs in house.

[00:14:10] Jordan: noted. our differentiators for POC: predictable latency SLOs, built-in batching/caching to lower per-token cost, and options for private deployment.

[00:14:30] Priya: risks: if we need an on-prem box in EU for some customers, the lead time is longer (4–8 weeks) depending on procurement. we should flag that in timeline.

[00:14:50] Carlos: makes sense. also want to validate quality regressions when quantizing — sometimes you see subtle drops.

[00:15:00] Priya: we'll include quantization A/Bs in benchmarks: int8/4/qat as needed; report will show quality delta.

[00:15:20] Jordan: ok let's capture explicit acceptance criteria for POC: 1) latency p95 < 350ms for interactive flows in hosted/dedicated EU region, or private if needed. 2) throughput sustained at 3x peak for 60 minutes without errors. 3) relevance delta < 5% on labeled set. 4) integration with SSO + audit logs. 5) documented KMS approach for EU customers.

[00:16:05] Rina: that looks right. can you send a one-pager with those criteria and the proposed timeline?

[00:16:10] Jordan: yes, we'll send a POC one-pager.

[00:16:25] Priya: next, practical steps and ownership: we'll provision a sandbox hosted env for microbenchmarks; if results are promising we'll provision a dedicated reserved pool in eu-west; and parallel work on contract/compliance.

[00:16:45] Carlos: for the dedicated pool are there minimum commitments?

[00:16:50] Jordan: yes reserved capacity typically has a monthly commit; exact size depends on throughput requirements — we'll provide a pricing sketch.

[00:17:05] Aisha: would you recommend starting with hosted then move to dedicated or go straight to dedicated for EU data?

[00:17:15] Priya: pragmatic approach: start hosted for non-restricted customers to iterate quickly; use dedicated in-region for EU customers or private if KMS/contract requires it. we can run a small dedicated pool as a pilot for EU while keeping other traffic on hosted.

[00:17:45] Liam: fine, we prefer staged rollout.

[00:17:50] Jordan: any blockers on our side to run the benchmark?

[00:17:55] Carlos: legal review for hosted API access and a sandbox contract for keys; Rina will lead on compliance signoff.

[00:18:05] Rina: yes we'll need the SOC2 and a data processing addendum.

[00:18:15] Jordan: we'll attach those.

[00:18:25] Priya: timeline recap: sandbox hosted microbenchmark in week 1-2, results and tuning week 3, dedicated pilot spin-up week 4-5, integration & compliance week 6-8, pilot run week 9.

[00:18:45] Carlos: what's our success gate to expand beyond pilot?

[00:18:50] Liam: if latency and quality metrics meet acceptance and ops shows stable runbook and logs, we'll expand to more customers.

[00:19:00] Jordan: let's capture concrete next steps — i'll read them out.

[00:19:05] Jordan: action items: jordan share security pack and POC one-pager; priya provide benchmark harness and preliminary cost model; mnemosyne to share labeled prompts and traces; schedule on-prem technical deep dive if procurement for EU private is needed.

[00:19:30] Carlos: we'll aim to get labeled set and traces within 5 business days.

[00:19:40] Rina: we'll review SOC2 and DPA and revert within a week.

[00:19:50] Priya: any final questions?

[00:20:00] Aisha: just one — do you support per-tenant encryption keys?

[00:20:05] Priya: yes for private and dedicated we can support per-tenant keys via KMS; for hosted it's more limited.

[00:20:15] Jordan: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.

[00:20:25] Carlos: thanks all.

[00:20:30] End of recorded portion — post-call notes: agreement to run hosted microbenchmark first, and to consider dedicated EU pilot in parallel. Risks: legal timeline for hosted access and procurement for private hardware.

Note: transcription contains some artifacts (e.g., "k v cache" vs "KV cache") and occasional mis-attribution.
